Posted October 3, 2002

Colin Davies Hearing Delayed Until Thursday Because Prosecution Now Has " New Evidence " That George Orwell Could Understand. Supporters Not Optimistic About Release Before September.

Yesterday began with the disturbing news that Colin Davies had been convicted on all counts. This was always a very real possibility because there was not muchin question about the facts.

However, Colin had been acquitted twice before by juries using their right to reject the implementation of unjust laws. The first time Colin was growing for his own use and the second time he was growing and distributing to other patients.

Nonetheless, the police were caught again in several lies about other defendants, and there had been a parade of witnesses who were patients who told the court about how Colin had helped them. So, some observers were optimistic.

Unfortunately, Colin's and our -- luck ran out this time, as did the jury's compassion. He was convicted on all counts and today he was sentenced to three years in prison. Such a harsh sentence was especially disturbing, given Colin's serious problems arising from a broken spine. When he was convicted everyone hoped that he would just be sentence to time served. He has been held in Strangeways Prison since last November, except for about six weeks in May and June, when was released on absurd bail conditions. (He could not return to his own apartment, and was re-imprisoned when he was caught at his flat.)

During all of this time, The Dutch Experience remained open. Today, shortly after Colin was sentenced, fifty heavily armed Greater Manchester Police, stormed the place, ordered the patients out and closed it down. As had happened in the past, the members regrouped and reopened the place once more.

The police returned again and kicked everyone out. In an absurd situation, Colin's younger brother was arrested for being in the loo, and therefore unable to respond with sufficient speed to a competing evacuation order.

It is unlikely that the police will allow the patients to regroup again. They will be sent back to their dark little rooms to suffer alone. That way we can pretend that they do not exist.

That will make at least some of the Greater Manchester Police happy. Today's Independent reported, Detectives in Manchester could scarcely hide their delight yesterday when, at the third attempt, they won drugs convictions against the owner of Britain's first Amsterdam-style cannabis café.

I have been very disturbed that there had been almost no media coverage of Colin's being held prior to his trial, or of the trial itself.

There was plenty to report. After all, this is one of those stories with both human interest and topicality. The UK has supposedly been engaged in a debate on cannabis policies, including medical access, which an overwhelming majority support.

I was especially puzzled by the lack of coverage by Colin's hometown paper, the Stockport Express. It is now clear that they would not report it, because they did not want to tell their readers about the patients who testified in Colin's behalf.

In all of the time that I have been watching the media malfeasance on this issue, I have seen very little reporting as vile as their stories on Colin's conviction and sentencing. Remember that there was no question about the facts in the trial. The only question was whether this jury would acquit him as the other two had.

Juries are almost always told by the prosecutor that they must convict on the facts, and cannot acquit just because they feel human sympathy, which is a danger to the state. Consequently, his being convicted does not necessarily mean that the jury did not believe that he was sincere.

Now here are yesterday's and today's venom doses from The Stockport Express:

Cannabis conman
Fromhttp://www.stockportexpress.co.uk/news/index.cfm?story=05full.html
CANNABIS conman Colin Davies has today (Wednesday) been found guilty of international drug trafficking.

The boss of Britain's first cannabis café sold the drug with coffee, claiming it was for medicinal purposes for people who needed pain relief.

In reality, The Dutch Experience café was a smokescreen. A jury at Minshull Street Crown Court took four hours deliberation before finding him guilty of trafficking narcotics between Holland and Dover, on top of a number of other drug-related offences.
(MarijuanaNews note: Narcotics? There has been no allegation of any thing other than cannabis being involved. The term narcotic is sometimes used generically, but very incorrectly to describe all illegal drugs, even stimulants, the exact opposite of a narcotic. The purpose is usually to deceive and to slander.)

Davies, 44, of Romney Tower, Reddish is now to be sentenced at a later date.

He - along with 13 others - was arrested in a police raid in September last year, following a public display of flouting drug laws at the Reddish café.

Soon after customs seized 18,000 pounds of cannabis at Dover connected to Davies.
(MarijuanaNews note: No, not 18,000 pounds of cannabis, but 18,000 UK Pounds worth of cannabis, weighing about nine pounds. The con artists who pose as journalists at the Stockport Express get paid in Pounds, which is proof that they are con artists.

Even that 18,000UKP valuation is probably high, but the disastrous UK drugs policies have driven down the value of hard drugs, while keeping cannabis relatively expensive, which is why the patients need someone to sell cannabis to them at discount prices the way Colin did.)

A raid on Davies' home found 90 grammes of cannabis and £3,000 in cash at a time when he was claiming just over £50 per week disability allowance.

Davies was found guilty of importing drugs, being concerned with the supply of drugs, possession with intent and permitting the premises to be used for smoking cannabis. He'd denied all charges.

Others in court included:

Stephen Caveney, 47, of Rishworth Close, Offerton has been convicted of possessing cannabis with intent.

Robin Wright, 45, of Duncan Road, Longsight was found guilty of permitting premises to be used for smoking the drug.

Andrew Young, 30, of Reddish Road, Stockport, and Phillip Rainford, 34, of Millgate, Stockport were acquitted of drugs charges.

While awaiting trial, Davies has become a figurehead for legalise dope campaigners.

Davies first hit the headlines in 1998 when he claimed to take marijuana to combat pain following a fall three years earlier. He was acquitted of unlawful possession.
(MarijuanaNews note: His spine was broken. He is prescribed morphine for the chronic pain. There is no question about his injuries.)

He then set up a nationwide 'cannabis co-operative' which involved him selling the drug to other members. He was subsequently charged but cleared again.

In 2000, he hit the national headlines when he gave a bouquet of marijuana to the Queen during her visit to Salford's Lowry centre.

Drug dealer Davies gets three year jailing

CANNABIS conman Colin Davies has been jailed for three years today (Thursday).

Colin Davies - the brains behind an international marijuana trafficking organisation - was found guilty of several drugs-related charges at court yesterday.

Davies, 44, of Romney Towers, Brinnington - and the boss of Reddish's Amsterdam-style Dutch Experience café - learned his fate at Minshull Street Crown Court 24 hours later.

His arrest 13 months ago came during a media frenzy as he openly smoked the drug in front of arresting officers. The matter has remained high profile ever since.

But in reality, he was also a drug dealer who used his café and public beliefs as a front for drug dealing.

A spokesman for Greater Manchester Police said dealers, like Davies, are not above the law.

The spokesman said: " GMP will continue to enforce drug laws in the same way that all forces are required to do so, until changes are made through our democratic institutions.

" No reputable police force would tolerate the illegal sale of drugs in their area, and although we acknowledge there is much debate and discussion about the decriminalisation of cannabis, the police service and the criminal justice system would be brought into disrepute if people were allowed to flagrantly break the law.

" No-one has yet suggested that drug dealers who sell illegal substances for substantial revenues, which Colin Davies has been convicted of, are exempt from the law. "

Supporters of Davies are in uproar over the conviction.

Speaking outside the court yesterday (Wednesday), Davies' father Colin senior, who along with wife Elsie has supported his son throughout, slammed the verdict.

Mr Davies said: " Colin has been a martyr to the cause. He has put his head on the line but it has just not happened the way he wanted.

" I'm very disappointed with the verdict and very surprised.

" Colin just wants to help and wants people to be able to grow their own plants.

" Colin will be feeling very disappointed but I'm sure it's something he would do again. "

Local Euro MP Chris Davies criticised the conviction of the Brinnington man.

He said: " Colin Davies is a martyr who has led the challenge to the ridiculous laws on cannabis.

" I have no doubt that in the course of time his actions will be entirely vindicated. "

He added: " Now that the Home Secretary has signalled the intention to downgrade the law on cannabis, this conviction makes the legal system look farcical, it is like a throwback to another time. "
(MarijuanaNews note: Chris Davies, no kin to Colin, is a good man. One of the few politicians that I have met who really gets it. However, if this conviction makes the legal system look farcical think how grotesque this kind of reporting makes journalism look.

Ironically, yesterday, when the Stockport Express was saying that Colin claimed to take marijuana to combat pain following a fall, the Telegraph reported, Low doses of cannabis can relieve severe pain for people with multiple sclerosis and spinal cord injuries, the largest clinical trial into the drug has found.

To make matters even more surreal, this morning the Daily Telegraph carried a story with the headline:

Britain has one of the highest numbers of drug addicts in the European Union, according to an official survey.

The report by the shows Britain also has the highest number of people who admit to trying amphetamine, as well as the highest number who have used cannabis.

About 11 per cent of people questioned in Britain told researchers they had tried amphetamine, compared with 1 per cent to 6 per cent among other EU members.

Britain had 6.7 " problem drug users " per 1,000 - those who inject or are long-term users of opiates, cocaine or amphetamine, often committing crime to feed their expensive habits.

Only Italy, Portugal and Luxembourg had more drug addicts and Britain was one of seven EU countries where the number of " problem users " was expected to increase.

The Netherlands, which has the most liberal drugs laws in Europe, had the lowest number of addicts with 2.6 per 1,000.
See
New Dutch Study on " Licit and illicit drug use in the Netherlands " Shows Why International Anti-Dutch Prohibitionist Propaganda Campaign Is Vital to Drug Warriors. How Ideology Works.

(MarijuanaNews note: Anotherarticle on the EMCDDA report in today's Independentunintentionally added to the absurdity:

The report said that the presence of drugs had " fundamentally changed prison reality " , with the level of use of some form of illicit narcotics put as high as 86 per cent, and routinely at more than 50 per cent among inmates. But it also pointed out that most drug users in prison tended to stop or cut down when they were released. The reason given was that they no longer had access to the drugs.

We really could not make this up.)
